conventions.convention: The flux is σ = −∇u, div σ = f; the least-squares residual is (σ + ∇u, div σ − f), with the scalar trial factor in H1_0.

All DPG fields are real. Skeleton spaces are ranges of global H1_0 and H(div) traces with global lift-infimum norms; boundary pairings use cell-outward normals. Tests carry the full broken H(div) × H1 graph norm.
In dimension two, R(a,b) = (−b,a), scalar curl is ∂1w2 − ∂2w1, and the tangential orientation is t = Rn.
Practical Riesz solves use exact real Gram entries and exact arithmetic. Dependent generating families return singular-test-matrix; an empty family returns zero.
The practical family is two-dimensional: P1 vector/scalar volume trials, continuous P2 scalar skeleton traces, P1 normal skeleton traces, and broken P3 vector/scalar tests.
The continuous graph result covers connected bounded Lipschitz polyhedra in dimensions two and three, including holes; its constants may depend on the fixed domain but not mesh size.

Least-squares best approximation assumes AC and Countable Choice through its weak Poisson supplier; the topology-free DPG lifting assumes Countable Choice and uses a separate real Lax–Milgram argument.

load_bearing.statement: There is a bounded linear map R: V′ → U such that BR = I and ||R|| ≤ C_*, independently of the mesh, on every bounded connected Lipschitz polyhedron in dimensions two and three under Countable Choice; no simple-connectivity or connected-boundary hypothesis is imposed.

Under Countable Choice, the stated triangular P1/P2/P1 trial family has an element-local Fortin map into P3 vector/scalar tests, with a mesh-independent broken graph bound, scalar mean preservation, ||v − Πgrad_3v||L2(K) ≤ Ch_K||∇v||L2(K), and b(w_h,y − Πy) = 0.
Assume Countable Choice. In the spaces of the ultraweak formulation, if b(x,y) = 0 for every broken test on a bounded connected Lipschitz domain, then x = 0.
Under Countable Choice, for every open D the weak normal trace H(div;D) → (H1(D)/H1_0(D))′ is onto, and every functional L has a lift τ with ||τ||H(div) ≤ ||L||.

Under Countable Choice, the elementwise scalar and normal trace maps have real Hilbert quotient ranges with global lift-infimum norms; compatible normal traces are conservative on interior facets in the weak distributional sense.
Under Countable Choice on a bounded connected Lipschitz planar domain, R(δσ,δu) = (δσ + ∇δu, div δσ) is injective on H(div) × H1_0 and its norm is equivalent to the product graph norm.

Under the stated continuous invertibility and Fortin hypotheses, for every discrete approximation the practical residual satisfies β²||x − x̃_h||U² ≤ η² + (||Π||η + osc(F))² and η ≤ ||b||||x − x̃_h||U; the stated Poisson oscillation is bounded by cell-average h-weighted L2 data oscillation.
